identity.title: Revenue Guarantees of No-Swap-Regret Dynamics in First Price Auctions

problem.claim: The paper studies revenue in discrete first-price auctions under approximate correlated equilibrium, with bids on a grid from 0 to 1 in increments of 1/k.

contributions.claim: It gives a revenue lower bound for every ε-approximate correlated equilibrium: at least v₂ − Θ(1/k) − Θ(εk²), where v₂ is the second-highest valuation.
It establishes polynomial convergence rates for revenue generated by no-swap-regret bidders in first-price auctions.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their results provide the first polynomial convergence rates for revenue generated by no-swap-regret bidders in first-price auctions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that any ε-approximate correlated equilibrium achieves revenue at least v₂ − Θ(1/k) − Θ(εk²).
The authors report that with optimal swap regret O(√(kT)), time-averaged revenue reaches at least v₂ − Θ(1/k) − Θ(ε) after O(k⁵/ε²) rounds.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper specifies discrete first-price auctions with bids restricted to a 1/k grid.
It derives a lower bound on revenue for ε-approximate correlated equilibria in terms of the second-highest valuation and discretization and approximation errors.
It presents the result as the first polynomial convergence-rate statement for no-swap-regret bidders.
It instantiates the guarantee for optimal swap regret, giving a time-averaged revenue bound and round complexity.

source_observation.claim: The abstract fixes the auction discretization before stating both the equilibrium revenue bound and the no-swap-regret convergence rate, retaining explicit dependence on k and ε.

lessons.interpretation: A concrete parameterized setting can make the scope and tradeoffs of a theoretical guarantee legible.
lessons.application: When presenting a dynamics theorem, define the action discretization first and report how approximation and runtime scale with its parameters.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the target problem is inherently continuous or when discretization materially changes the phenomenon of interest.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the assumptions on valuations, bidder behavior, or the precise relationship between ε-approximate correlated equilibrium and swap-regret dynamics.
The constants hidden by Θ notation and the conditions under which the stated round complexity applies are not given.
The first-polynomial-rate priority claim is author-reported and not independently checked.
